text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Up to 79 Duty Credit Certificates, allowing Namibian companies to import goods with a full rebate on customs duties, could have been issued fraudulantly during the first months of 1997, an investigation by the Namibian newspaper has found.
- The Namibian government must accelerate the scaling down of the civil service in order to curtail rising costs of its bureaucracy, a senior economist said.
- The government's bureaucracy is killing Namibia, Standard Bank economist Philip Clayton says, calling for an immediate cut in the civil service.
